key_changes_summary: Definition of culpable homicide preserved verbatim from IPC Section 299 with modernized numbering.
Substantive definition of murder preserved; reorganized with refined clauses and updated statutory cross-references.
Sub-section (1) retains death or life imprisonment for murder. Sub-section (2) introduces a new specific aggravated offence for mob lynching / murder committed by 5 or more on identity grounds.

Sub-section (1) increases maximum term for rash/negligent driving death from 2 to 5 years. Sub-section (2) introduces hit-and-run provision punishable with up to 10 years for escaping without reporting.
Brand new statutory chapter codifying Organised Crime (extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, cyber-crime syndicates) directly in general penal law.
Brand new provision codifying Terrorist Acts threatening sovereignty, integrity, or security of India within general criminal code.
Consolidates definition (former 378) and punishment (former 379). Adds a progressive proviso: mandatory Community Service for first-time petty theft where stolen value is under Rs. 5,000.
Explicitly codifies 'Snatching' (chain/mobile snatching) as a distinct aggravated statutory theft category punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment and fine.
Consolidates definition of criminal breach of trust (IPC 405) and punishment (IPC 406) into a single unified section, increasing sentence up to 5 years.
Consolidates cheating (IPC 415), simple cheating punishment (IPC 417), and aggravated cheating with inducement to deliver property (IPC 420) into subsections of Section 318.
Consolidates criminal intimidation definition and sentence into Section 351.
Consolidates defamation definition and penalty. Introduces Community Service as an alternative statutory sentencing option alongside simple imprisonment.
Mandates recording reasons for arrest under 7 years; introduces special safeguard requiring prior DSP permission before arresting senior citizens (above 60) for minor offences (< 3 years).
Mandates audio-video electronic recording (videography) of entire search, seizure, and witness signing process with immediate electronic dispatch to Magistrate.
Codifies e-FIR with 3-day verification, Zero FIR across territorial limits, and preliminary inquiry (up to 14 days) for offences punishable with 3 to 7 years imprisonment.
Police final report (chargesheet) can be submitted electronically; strict statutory 60-day completion deadline for sexual offences and POCSO.
Extends mandatory bail for undertrials: first-time offenders who have never been convicted in past are eligible for mandatory bail upon completing 1/3rd (instead of 1/2) of maximum detention term.
Prohibition of confessions made to police officers preserved verbatim.
Information leading to discovery of relevant fact/object in custody preserved verbatim.
Adds Explanation 3 clarifying that each electronic store, memory or media storing digital records qualifies directly as primary evidence.
Expressly confers full legal parity and enforceability on electronic and digital records alongside traditional physical documents.
Standardizes electronic record certificate requirements under Section 63(4) incorporating Schedule certificate format, simplifying verification standards established by Supreme Court jurisprudence.
